summary: node-helper 1.6.4 ships obfuscated require-time dropper that stages a socket.io C2 / Windows credential stealer
details: node-helper.js exports a benign-looking helper API followed by a heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io string-array) IIFE that executes at require() time. The IIFE creates a hidden directory under os.homedir(), writes a package.json declaring runtime dependencies axios, better-sqlite3, node-machine-id, socket.io-client, and on Windows @primno/dpapi, then spawns npm install into that directory and executes a staged loader written to disk. On Windows the dropper additionally writes a main.vbs that uses WScript.Shell.Run with window-mode 0 and launches the node payload via %WINDIR%\system32\wscript.exe to run hidden from the console. The staged dependency set (socket.io-client for duplex C2, node-machine-id for host fingerprinting, better-sqlite3 for browser/keyring database reads, @primno/dpapi for Windows DPAPI-protected secret decryption) is the canonical shape of a remote-controlled credential and wallet stealer. Package metadata (author 'Blake Embrey', README badges linking to blakeembrey/node-helper) impersonates a legitimate maintainer's identity as a cover story. Requiring the module on any platform runs the dropper; on Windows the payload is launched with a hidden window.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
